summary: Pro-rated plan migration resulted in mismatched per-token rate and duplicate credit on March invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer migrated from self-serve to a Dedicated plan on 2026-03-05 (commit: 50k tokens/month reserved). After migration the customer received the March invoice dated 2026-03-07 showing two anomalies: (1) Usage during 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05 was billed at legacy self-serve per-token rate despite expectation of pro-rated dedicated pricing applied from 2026-03-05; (2) A one-time pro-rate credit was listed twice (duplicate credit entries) producing an incorrect net credit leading to -$1,220 shown then later corrected by customer-facing portal adjustment.
Impact: Billing confusion and temporary negative balance; customer paused feature rollout until cleared. Revenue impact is limited but customer-facing trust impact is high for a strategic dedicated-tier customer.
Timeline: 2026-03-05: plan migration processed via Console -> Account -> Billing. 2026-03-07: March invoice generated. 2026-03-08: Customer reported via in-app support. 2026-03-10: Ticket opened and assigned to billing. 2026-03-11: Billing engineering confirmed reproducer. 2026-03-12: Manual credit issued and audit log created. 2026-03-13: Permanent fix merged to billing service.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a self-serve account with ongoing usage for a month. 2) Mid-cycle (day X) upgrade to Dedicated via Console (select reserved commit). 3) Trigger billing run for that month or simulate invoice generation with same cutover date. 4) Inspect invoice line items for pre-cutover usage and pro-rate credit entries.
Observed behavior: Invoice shows pre-cutover usage at old per-token rate. Pro-rate credit for the transition appears twice: once in invoice_line_items (as expected) and once as a separate adjustment record (duplicate). The billing calc applied the dedicated rate to post-cutover usage correctly but did not apply the dedicated discount to pre-cutover usage that should have been pro-rated from the cutover time. Logs show two separate code paths creating the credit adjustment: (a) immediate pro-rate adjustment created when plan-change webhook processed; (b) invoice-generation reconciler also computed a pro-rate credit and appended it.
Expected behavior: One pro-rate credit equal to the pro-rated difference between old and new per-unit rates for the portion of the billing period that falls after migration, and pre-cutover usage billed at original rate only for hours prior to migration.
Attachments: invoice_2026-03-07.pdf (customer uploaded), billing_audit_2026-03-05-07.log (support extracted), console-screenshot-migration.png.
Additional notes: Customer quoted concern about double refunds if we issue manual credit without cancelling duplicate adjustment. Also asked for confirmation that future invoices will reflect dedicated pricing correctly.
comments: 2026-03-08 10:12 - Aisha Banerjee (Support): Customer submitted invoice PDF and account ID. They reported seeing a negative balance followed by a correction in the portal that was unexplained. Asked for invoice ID, migration timestamp, and org billing contact.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Marco Ruiz (Billing Eng): Assigned. Requested owner_id and backend migration webhook logs, plus whether migration was done via console or API. Asked SRE to pull billing run trace for 2026-03-07.

2026-03-11 14:20 - Priya Nair (SRE): Found reconciler trace: invoice-generator invoked pro-rate reconciliation step which computed a credit; separate plan-change webhook also created adjustment id adj_77f. Both adjustments were semantically identical. Reproducer attached. Hypothesis: webhook and reconciler both trigger when migration timestamp is present but dedupe key not set.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Marco Ruiz (Billing Eng): Issued manual reversal to neutralize duplicate adjustment (credit id adj_77f reversed). Created one-time account-level adjustment to correct net credit and sent transaction receipt to customer. Noted that pre-cutover usage still billed at legacy rate — will be addressed in fix.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Customer (NimbleChat billing contact, Jonah Li): Confirmed receipt of manual credit and happy with net effect. Asked us to confirm that future invoices will show dedicated pricing for post-migration usage.

2026-03-13 08:40 - Marco Ruiz (Billing Eng): Patch merged (github.com/redwood-inference/billing/commit/3a9b2f1) to add a dedupe key for pro-rate adjustments and to ensure invoice reconciler applies pro-rate only once and uses migration timestamp boundary to split usage. Deployed to staging; schedule for rollout to prod 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Created follow-up internal ticket INT-1149 to add e2e test coverage. Marking support ticket resolved and added resolution notes.
resolution_notes: Manual correction applied: duplicate adjustment adj_77f reversed and single corrective account-level adjustment issued. Customer notified and provided receipt. Root cause: missing deduplication between plan-change webhook and invoice-generation reconciler leading to two pro-rate adjustments. Permanent fix merged and scheduled; e2e tests added under INT-1149. Recommended follow-up: monitor next billing run (2026-04-07) for any residual discrepancies and confirm with customer after next invoice.
